Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $x=3{y}^{2}-{y}^{3}$ and the $y$-axis, as shown above. What integral gives the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis?
questions.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $y$-axis by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3{y}^{2}-{y}^{3} & =0 \\ {y}^{2}(3-y) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $y=0,\,3.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=3.$ 

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}yf(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}y(3{y}^{2}-{y}^{3})\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $x=5{y}^{3}-5{y}^{4}$ and the $y$-axis. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $y$-axis by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5{y}^{3}-5{y}^{4} & =0 \\ 5{y}^{3}(1-y) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $y=0$ and $y=1.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=1.$ 

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}yf(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}y(5{y}^{3}-5{y}^{4})\text{d}y \\  & =10\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{4}-{y}^{5})\text{d}y \\  & =10\pi ({\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{4}\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{5}\text{d}y) \\  & =10\pi ({\frac{{y}^{5}}{5}|}_{0}^{1}-{\frac{{y}^{6}}{6}|}_{0}^{1}) \\  & =10\pi ((\frac{1}{5}-0)-(\frac{1}{6}-0)) \\  & =10\pi (\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{6}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $x=-8+6y-{y}^{2}$ and the $y$-axis. What integral gives the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis?
questions.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $y$-axis by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-8+6y-{y}^{2} & =0 \\ {y}^{2}-6y+8 & =0 \\ (y-2)(y-4) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $y=2$ and $y=4.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=2$ to $y=4.$

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}yf(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{2}^{4}y(-8+6y-{y}^{2})\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $x={y}^{2}-5{y}^{3}$ and the $y$-axis. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $y$-axis by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-5{y}^{3} & =0 \\ {y}^{2}(1-5y) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $y=0$ and $y=\frac{1}{5}.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=\frac{1}{5}.$ 

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}yf(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1/5}y({y}^{2}-5{y}^{3})\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1/5}({y}^{3}-5{y}^{4})\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi ({\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}|}_{0}^{1/5}-5\cdot {\frac{{y}^{5}}{5}|}_{0}^{1/5}) \\  & =2\pi (\frac{1}{4\cdot {5}^{4}}-\frac{1}{{5}^{5}}) \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{{5}^{4}}(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{20\cdot {5}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6\,250}\end{aligned}
$$
